{"action":"final","query":{"op":"none","scope":null,"id":null,"text":null,"start":null,"end":null,"offset":null,"derived_op":null,"groupBy":null},"diagnosis":"The forward kernel forms powers and squared powers in the input dtype before reduction. This introduces low-precision rounding and overflow into normalization. Actual GPU evidence reports 23,541/32,768 mismatches for fp16 width 8192; the same-width fp32 control and width-128 fp16 control pass. These observations support a dtype-dependent numerical defect, but do not identify the precise overflowing intermediate. Widening before arithmetic repairs this defect. FP64 intermediates also accommodate sixth powers across the finite fp16/bf16/fp32 input range, where simply promoting to FP32 would still overflow. Output allocation and stores preserve shape/dtype, inputs remain untouched, and cached reciprocal standard deviations retain their existing meaning. FP64 arithmetic may reduce throughput. Compilation and held-out tests were unavailable; the attempted raw-record lookup failed, so citations refer to the supplied actual-device observation summaries. Backward numerical behavior is outside this repair.","locations":[{"source_id":"source-28","start_line":57,"end_line":87},{"source_id":"source-28","start_line":89,"end_line":98},{"source_id":"source-28","start_line":222,"end_line":255}],"citations":[{"case_id":"poly-02","evidence_ids":["observation-poly-02"]},{"case_id":"poly-03","evidence_ids":["observation-poly-03"]},{"case_id":"poly-00","evidence_ids":["observation-poly-00"]}],"edits":[{"source_id":"source-28","old":"    # Load input row
    X_row = tl.load(X_ptr + col_offsets, mask=mask, other=0.0)

    # Load weights and bias
    w0 = tl.load(W_ptr + 0)
    w1 = tl.load(W_ptr + 1)
    w2 = tl.load(W_ptr + 2)
    b = tl.load(B_ptr)","new":"    # Widen before forming powers. Even finite FP32 inputs can have sixth
    # powers outside FP32 range; FP64 covers the supported input range.
    X_row = tl.load(X_ptr + col_offsets, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float64)

    # Keep the weighted sum wide until the final output store.
    w0 = tl.load(W_ptr + 0).to(tl.float64)
    w1 = tl.load(W_ptr + 1).to(tl.float64)
    w2 = tl.load(W_ptr + 2).to(tl.float64)
    b = tl.load(B_ptr).to(tl.float64)"},{"source_id":"source-28","old":"    # Compute norm(x³): norm(u) = u * rsqrt(mean(u²) + eps)
    # Force fp32 eps: Inductor may use fp64 under torch.compile and tank throughput.
    eps = eps.to(tl.float32)

    mean_square_3 = tl.sum(X_pow3 * X_pow3, axis=0) / n_cols
    rstd_3 = rsqrt(mean_square_3 + eps)
    norm_x3 = X_pow3 * rstd_3

    # Compute norm(x²)
    mean_square_2 = tl.sum(X_pow2 * X_pow2, axis=0) / n_cols
    rstd_2 = rsqrt(mean_square_2 + eps)
    norm_x2 = X_pow2 * rstd_2

    # Compute norm(x)
    mean_square_1 = tl.sum(X_pow1 * X_pow1, axis=0) / n_cols
    rstd_1 = rsqrt(mean_square_1 + eps)
    norm_x1 = X_pow1 * rstd_1","new":"    # Keep powers, reductions, and denominators in FP64. Masked lanes are
    # zero, and the mean divides by the actual number of input columns.
    eps = eps.to(tl.float64)

    mean_square_3 = tl.sum(X_pow3 * X_pow3, axis=0) / n_cols
    rstd_3 = 1.0 / tl.sqrt(mean_square_3 + eps)
    norm_x3 = X_pow3 * rstd_3

    # Compute norm(x²)
    mean_square_2 = tl.sum(X_pow2 * X_pow2, axis=0) / n_cols
    rstd_2 = 1.0 / tl.sqrt(mean_square_2 + eps)
    norm_x2 = X_pow2 * rstd_2

    # Compute norm(x)
    mean_square_1 = tl.sum(X_pow1 * X_pow1, axis=0) / n_cols
    rstd_1 = 1.0 / tl.sqrt(mean_square_1 + eps)
    norm_x1 = X_pow1 * rstd_1"}]}
